title: BCentral journal
description: Draft of 2026-10-28. The data the app stores, exports and syncs to a hub. Entries are append-only and immutable; status is derived from status_change entries, never stored on the thing it describes. Every id is a ULID minted at creation, so objects can be created offline on any device and merged by union.

deviceId.description: The device this file or batch came from

publicKey.description: MeshCore node public key, 32 bytes as lowercase hex

clockTrust.description: How much the device's clock could be trusted when the timestamp was taken: synced over the network, set by hand by an operator, or neither

drill.description: Proposed, not decided: true for an exercise (øvelse)

registerEntry.description: One radio, bound to a person, a street and a role. Binding is done by hand; nothing here is inferred.

label.description: What the staff call it: a person's name, or 'radio #7' until handed out

origin.description: issued = handed out per street by the association; adhoc = from the stack kept at the staff; private = bought by the person

journalEntry.description: Common envelope. The type decides which payload fields apply; the oneOf below enforces it.

deviceSeq.description: Per-device running number, gap-free. Lets a reader see whether anything is missing from one device's run.

operator.description: Who at the staff recorded this

counterpartyId.description: Register entry of the other end

seqNo.description: The #n of an outgoing message, per recipient per device; see text-protocol.md

refersTo.description: Another entry (reply, status change, correction) or an incident (status change)

dedupeKey.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of '<sender public key hex>:<sender timestamp as decimal epoch seconds>:<text as received>'. Direct messages are encrypted to one companion, so no other device hears them; this key catches duplicate deliveries of the same message (a radio retry, a sync replay), not other devices' copies.

oneOf.description: message_out: staff → field. Numbered per text-protocol.md. Its status lives in status_change entries that refer to it.
message_in: field → staff, stored as received. refersTo is set only by the operator by hand. dedupeKey is required for transport=mesh.
note: anything the operator writes into the journal that is not a message — a phone call made, a decision, an observation.

status_change: the only way status ever changes. refersTo is a message_out (pending/sent/delivered/roger/given_up) or an incident (closed/reopened). A roger recorded from an incoming message also carries the incoming entry's id in text, or the operator's reason for a manual change.
correction: the entry refersTo was wrong; text says what is right. The original is never edited or removed.
